current_disclosures.section: Products, Market, and Sales > Product Technologies
current_disclosures.summary: DRAM products are volatile, low-latency memory devices used in various markets including data centers, PCs, and automotive. In 2025, the company began shipping the industry's first 1γ production node incorporating EUV lithography for improved efficiency, while the majority of DRAM bit production remained on the 1ß node. This portfolio includes specialized types such as High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) for AI and high-performance computing, Double Data Rate (DDR) including DDR5, Low-Power DRAM (LPDDR) for mobile devices, and Graphics DRAM (GDDR) for graphics-intensive applications.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center Segment Product Portfolio and Strategy
comparisons.peer_summary: The Data Center segment includes server-class CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, DPUs, FPGAs, SmartNICs, and Adaptive SoC products. The company leverages these technologies to address computational, visual data processing, and AI workload acceleration needs by enabling optimization of performance and power for diverse workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies address the intersection of performance and power efficiency in data center applications, though they focus on different component types. MU notes that LPDDR benefits are realized in the data center segment, while AMD describes its Data Center segment products (CPUs, GPUs, etc.) enabling the 'optimization of performance and power for a diverse set of workloads' to meet data center demands.

sentences.text: The benefits of LPDDR memory are being realized by many market segments including mobile, PC, automotive, and data center.
We leverage our technology to address the computational, visual data processing and AI workload acceleration needs in the data center market.
Different combinations of CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, FPGAs, SmartNICs, and Adaptive SoCs enable the optimization of performance and power for a diverse set of workloads.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company provides Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and GPS/GNSS solutions for mobile devices, including integrated combination chips and location platform services.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AVGO disclose products specifically engineered for mobile devices with an emphasis on low power consumption. MU describes LPDDR as engineered for mobile devices requiring low power and operating at lower voltage, while AVGO highlights its connectivity solutions for mobile devices including 'high performance, low power Wi-Fi chipsets' and 'low power' Bluetooth technology.

sentences.text: Low-Power DRAM ("LPDDR"): Engineered for mobile devices and applications requiring low power consumption.
LPDDR products generally operate at a lower voltage than standard DRAM products and are beneficial to any power conscious application.

• Connectivity Solutions: Our connectivity solutions include discrete and integrated Wi-Fi and Bluetooth solutions, and global positioning system/global navigation satellite system ("GPS/GNSS") receivers, designed for use in mobile devices including smartphones, tablets and wearable products.
We offer a family of high performance, low power Wi-Fi chipsets.
Bluetooth is a low power technology that enables direct connectivity between devices.

peer_results.rationale: The provided INT candidates focus on edge computing processor suites and data center CPU launches, emphasizing architectural details (NPU IP, E-cores) and manufacturing processes (Intel 3, Intel 7). These do not substantively compare to MU's disclosure on the specific electrical characteristics (low voltage, power consumption) and market applications of Low-Power DRAM technology.

The provided NVDA candidates describe broad data-center-scale architectures, full-stack computing infrastructure, and AI application deployment. These high-level strategic descriptions do not provide specific comparable facts regarding the power specifications or low-voltage engineering of memory products as discussed by MU.

comparisons.peer_summary: QCT's RF portfolio includes RFFE components for 5G and 4G LTE to improve performance and reduce power consumption. The company has integrated its Snapdragon platform with RFFE components to create Snapdragon 5G modem-RF products that use AI to maximize data speeds and performance.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and QCOM highlight power efficiency as a key attribute of their respective technologies for mobile and connected devices. MU states that LPDDR products 'operate at a lower voltage' and are beneficial for 'power conscious application', whereas QCOM notes its RF products are designed to 'reduce power consumption' and its modem-RF integration helps 'extend battery life'.

sentences.text: LPDDR products generally operate at a lower voltage than standard DRAM products and are beneficial to any power conscious application.

Our portfolio of RF products includes Qualcomm® RFFE components that are designed to simplify the RF front-end design for 5G, including sub-6 GHz and mmWave, as well as, for 4G LTE multimode devices, to reduce power consumption and to improve radio performance.

We have also integrated our Snapdragon platform with our RFFE components to create our Snapdragon 5G modem-RF products, a modem-to-antenna platform integrating AI to maximize data speeds and performance, support superior call connectivity and coverage and extend battery life.
